title: Budgeting, Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy (Finance & Legal)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Purpose:
This document defines Redwood Inference’s corporate policies and standard operating procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contracts and legal intake/approval, procurement processes, and revenue recognition and billing practices. The goal is to ensure consistent decision-making, strong internal controls, and compliance with accounting standards and legal obligations.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood Inference business units and subsidiaries globally for: budgeting and forecasting, vendor contracting, procurement of goods/services, issuance of purchase orders, invoicing and billing, and recognition of revenue. Exceptions require written approval from Finance (Director+) and Legal.

Key Definitions:
- Budget: Annual plan of expected revenues, expenses, headcount, and capital spend.
- Forecast: Rolling forward-looking view updated monthly/quarterly that replaces or supplements the budget.
- PO (Purchase Order): Formal authorization to purchase goods/services.
- RevRec: Revenue recognition under ASC 606 (or equivalent local GAAP).

1) Roles and Ownership
- Finance: Owns budgeting & forecasting process, GL mapping, revenue recognition, invoicing cadence, and audit artifacts.
- Legal: Owns contract terms, risk assessment, non-standard clause negotiation, and signature authority for legal exceptions.
- Procurement (Finance/Operations): Manages preferred vendor list, PO issuance, vendor onboarding checklist, and contract repository tagging.
- Requesting Team (Engineering/Product/Sales/etc.): Submits purchase requests, provides business justification, and confirms receipt of goods/services.
- Approvers: Specified below in approval thresholds.

2) Budgeting Process (Annual)
Overview:
- Budgeting cadence: Annual planning begins in October for the next fiscal year. Final budget approved by the Board by the last business day of December.
- Owners: Each org (Engineering, Product, Sales, GtM, SRE, Research, Ops) submits a line-item budget and headcount plan.
- Templates: Finance provides a standardized budgeting template (sheets) with GL mappings and required justification fields.

Steps:
1. Oct 1 – Oct 15: Finance issues budget templates and guiding assumptions (growth rates, price inflation, hiring freezes).
2. Oct 16 – Nov 15: Teams submit draft budgets with supporting narratives and risk scenarios.
3. Nov 16 – Dec 10: Cross-functional review cycle; Finance consolidates and runs scenario analyses.
4. Dec 11 – Dec 20: Executive review and adjustments.
5. Dec 21 – Dec 31: Board approval and version lock.

Controls and Targets:
- Budget variance target: operating expense actuals should be within +/-5% of budget on a quarterly basis; material variances (>10%) require a remediation plan.
- Capital approvals: CAPEX > $250k requires CFO and CEO sign-off.

3) Forecasting (Rolling)
- Cadence: Monthly rolling forecast; deep quarterly forecast review with leadership.
- Drivers: Headcount, ARR/usage metrics, model-serving capacity costs, committed cloud spend, and sales pipeline conversion rates.
- Variance analysis: Finance publishes a monthly variance pack highlighting drivers > $25k.

4) Contracts and Legal Process
Objectives: Standardize contracting, reduce legal risk, and ensure proper revenue/billing terms.

Intake and Triage:
- All customer and vendor contracts must be submitted via the Contract Intake Form (internal link) and assigned a contract ID.
- Legal triages requests within 2 business days.

Standard Terms and Templates:
- Use company-approved templates: SaaS Customer Master Agreement (CMA), Reseller Agreement, MSAs for Dedicated/Private deployments, Professional Services Statement of Work (SOW), Vendor Master Agreement.
- Standard commercial terms: 12 month term default, auto-renew unless opted out 30 days prior, payment terms Net 30, liability cap = greater of $1M or total fees paid in 12 months.

Negotiation and Risk Review:
- Low-risk (standard, < $100k ARR or procurement value): Legal review waived if using template and checkbox completed; Finance must approve billing terms.
- Medium/high-risk (non-standard terms, > $100k, international data restrictions, security exceptions): Legal + Finance + Security review.

Signature and Execution:
- Authorized signatories: Legal Counsel and Finance Director must countersign commercial exceptions; standard template agreements may be e-signed by Sales Director for deals < $250k.
- Execution method: DocuSign (preferred) or company-authorized wet signatures when required by counterparty.

Contract Repository and Lifecycle:
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (DocuSign + SharePoint link) within 3 business days and tagged with contract ID, owner, renewal date, and billing terms.
- Renewal notifications: Automated alerts at 90/60/30 days pre-renewal to contract owner and Finance.

Change Control:
- Amendments must reference original contract ID and be countersigned by the same authorizing signatories as the original.

5) Procurement Procedures
Purpose: Ensure cost-effective purchasing, vendor due diligence, and segregation of duties.

Thresholds and Approvals:
- Purchases <= $5,000: Requesting manager approval.
- Purchases > $5,000 and <= $50,000: Department head + Procurement/Finance approval.
- Purchases > $50,000 and <= $250,000: Procurement, Finance Director approval, and Legal if contract required.
- Purchases > $250,000: CFO + CEO approval and Legal review for contracts.

Preferred Vendor Program:
- Procurement maintains an approved vendor list with pre-negotiated terms for common categories (cloud infra, GPU vendors, software licenses, professional services).
- For strategic vendors (> $100k annual spend) run an RFP process every 24 months.

PO and Invoice Process:
1. Submit purchase request with justification and cost center.
2. Procurement validates vendor and issues PO (PO required for purchases > $5,000).
3. Goods/services received and confirmed by requestor.
4. Vendor invoice submitted to AP with PO number. AP matches invoice to PO and receipt and processes payment per terms.

Emergency Purchases:
- Emergency procurement (e.g., critical infrastructure outage) can bypass PO requirement but must be documented and retroactively approved by Procurement and Finance within 5 business days.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (minimum):
- W-9 / local tax form, proof of insurance (when applicable), completed security/data handling questionnaire if vendor will access sensitive data, payment terms, and primary contact.

6) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies
Accounting Framework:
- Redwood follows ASC 606 principles (identify contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price, recognize revenue when/as performance obligations are satisfied). Local GAAP equivalents apply for non-US entities.

Revenue Streams and Recognition Rules:
- Hosted API (Usage-based): Revenue recognized as usage occurs (over time) based on metered tokens/units billed. Monthly invoicing; revenue recognized in the month the usage occurred.
- Dedicated Reserved Capacity (Committed): For multi-month/annual reserved capacity contracts, revenue is recognized ratably over the committed term. Upfront prepayments are recorded as deferred revenue and amortized.
- Private/Enterprise Licensing (Platform + Services): Platform subscription recognized over the subscription period. Professional services are recognized upon milestone completion or transfer of control as defined in the contract.
- One-time Implementation Fees: If the implementation does not create a separate, transferable good or service, fees are recognized over the subscription term as they are not distinct. If distinct, recognize on completion.

Billing & Invoicing:
- Default billing cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage and recurring services, Net 30.
- Annual prepayment: Recognize as deferred revenue and amortize monthly over the service term.
- Billing disputes: Customer has 30 days from invoice date to dispute; undisputed portion is payable per terms. Credit memos issued by Finance after investigation.

Deferred Revenue & Journal Guidance (examples):
- Customer prepays $120,000 for 12 months on Jan 1: Dr Cash 120,000; Cr Deferred Revenue 120,000. Monthly recognition: Dr Deferred Revenue 10,000; Cr Revenue 10,000.
- Usage invoice $15,000 for January usage, billed Feb 5, Net 30: Recognize revenue for January usage in January; record accounts receivable when invoice issued.

Revenue Cutover & Migration:
- For contract changes (upgrades/downgrades), Finance and Revenue Operations will calculate pro-rated adjustments and issue appropriate credits or additional invoices.

7) Controls, Compliance, and Audit
- Segregation of duties: Purchase requestor may not approve their own payments. Contract negotiator may not be principal approver for the same contract’s finance terms.
- Audit evidence: Procurement files, signed contracts, approved POs, invoices, and receipts must be retained for 7 years.
- Internal audit: Finance to facilitate annual internal audit and external audit requests.
- Tax compliance: Finance will validate VAT/GST requirements for international customers and ensure correct invoice formats and tax treatment.

8) KPIs and Monitoring
- Budget variance (quarterly): target within +/-5%.
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): target < 45 days.
- Percentage of spend with preferred vendors: target > 70%.
- PO compliance rate (purchases > $5k): target > 95%.

9) Exceptions and Escalation
- Non-standard contractual or procurement exceptions must be documented and approved by Legal and Finance Director.
- Material accounting judgment exceptions (e.g., new revenue model) require CFO and external auditor consultation.
